course_name_original: Análisis y Diseño de Sistemas Eléctricos
course_name_en: Analysis and Design of Electrical Systems
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of single-phase and three-phase circuit theory.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and ability for the analysis and design of electrical power generation, transmission, and distribution systems.
Describe the composition of electrical power systems and the associated technologies at all stages: generation, transmission, and distribution.
Calculate the operating variables of an electrical system under normal and anomalous operating conditions.
Differentiate the various protection devices involved in electricity distribution and transmission networks.

syllabus_topics: Three-phase short circuit in synchronous machine
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices (case studies, group work, simulation programs)

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (application of content through a practical case, submitted in writing)

assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in the final exam. The final grade is calculated as (0.8 * Final Exam) + (0.2 * Practical Work). If the minimum is not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. The grade for the practical work will be kept for extraordinary calls. If the practical work was not submitted in the ordinary call, it can be submitted for the extraordinary call.
bibliography: Glover, J.D., Overbye, T.J., Sarma, M.S., Birchfield, A.B.: Power System Analysis and Design. Cengage Learning, 2023, 7th edition.
Gómez-Expósito, A., Conejo, A.J., Cañizares, C.: Electric Energy Systems: Analysis and Operation. CRC Press, 2018, 2nd edition.
institution: Universidad de Oviedo - Máster Universitario en Ingeniería Industrial (EPI Gijón)
